content.summary_of_the_paper: The manuscript proposes cell type classification methods using single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNS-seq) data based on self-attention networks. The first method, called “Capsule attention network”, first calculates multiple embeddings for each cell (a vector of length of the number of genes) using different fully connected (FC) layers, and finds new representations of the embeddings using a single-ahead self-attention layer. The final prediction is done by a convolution layer followed by a FC layer. The second method, called “Cell-Gene Representation Attention Network (CGRAN)” is proposed to encode ‘cell-gene’ or ‘gene-gene’ associations. It first finds cell or gene embeddings using SVD decomposition or NMF and finds new representations using two a multi-head local attention layers, where the local attention refers to the block diagonal structure of the (local) attention weight matrix. The authors also provide the interesting interpretations (e.g., associations between cell types and genes) from the attention weights.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
1. Defining the attention weight matrix (which encodes interactions between genes) looks interesting. It also provides a way to identify genes that are associated with cell types by the same attention networks. 
2. The manuscript is easy to read and understand. 

Weaknesses
1. The novelty of the proposed methods look limited as the proposed methods are direct extensions of the self-attention mechanism. 
2. I have a concern about the experimental settings (please correct me if I misunderstood). Based on the description, it seems that the performance evaluation was done a single time after each data was randomly split to training and testing data sets. If this was true, the submission has issues with reproducibility. If not, the authors should update the experiments section to explicitly state how the performance was evaluated (for example, using cross validation?) and include some additional statistics of the performance of each method (for example, standard deviation).

I have some questions about what I did not fully understand. 
1. About eq. 4. The single cell RNA sequencing data might be very sparse due to dropout. I am not sure if Mean square error is suitable for this type of data. 
2. Section 4-2: “Attention mask matrix is a … The first line and row of the attention mask matrix are filed with zero”. It is not clear why the attention weights between a cell and genes are set to zero. Then, how can we interpret cell-gene attention weights in Section 5-2
3. Section 5-2 “We then compare these highly differential genes with the acknowledged marker genes and find out that they match with each other”. The manuscript does not include any tables or figures to support this sentence. 
4. Figure 5: The differential genes of each cell type in the figure are different from those in Figure 4. Specially, B or NK cells. Only subsets are displayed in Figure 5. Is it because those missing genes are in the same group (by the uniform grouping or K means)? 

Quality
The manuscript is overall well written. It is easy to read. 

Novelty & Reproducibility
Please see “Strength and Weaknesses”
content.summary_of_the_review: I think the manuscript is an interesting application paper using single-cell RNA sequencing to classify cell types. However, the novelty of the proposed methods looks limited and there seem to be some flaws in the experiments.

Dear Reviewer,

We thank you for the time and efforts reviewing our paper. We have received some valuable and constructive feedbacks from you to improve our paper. Here we will address your concerns.

Concern 2: The authors should update the experiments section to explicitly state how the performance was evaluated.

Reply : Please refer to Reviewer arZA concern 3.

Concern 3: About eq. 4. The single cell RNA sequencing data might be very sparse due to dropout. I am not sure if Mean square error is suitable for this type of data.

Reply : The matrix factorization process serves as an initialization of the gene and cell embeddings, which is not playing a key role since the embeddings are later updated through the attention model. Because our model requires no assumptions or data imputation, the factorization by MSE loss could preserve the original scRNA-seq matrix without prior knowledge or assumptions.

Concern 4: Section 4-2: “Attention mask matrix is a … The first line and row of the attention mask matrix are filed with zero”. It is not clear why the attention weights between a cell and genes are set to zero. Then, how can we interpret cell-gene attention weights in Section 5-2?

Reply : This is an error in our original version. Thanks for pointing it out. We have corrected in our new version.

Concern 5: Section 5-2 “We then compare these highly differential genes with the acknowledged marker genes and find out that they match with each other”. The manuscript does not include any tables or figures to support this sentence.

Reply :Please refer to arZA concern 4.

Concern 6: Figure 5: The differential genes of each cell type in the figure are different from those in Figure 4. Specially, B or NK cells. Only subsets are displayed in Figure 5. Is it because those missing genes are in the same group (by the uniform grouping or K means)?

Reply : The marker genes listed in Figure 5(last version, Figure 10 in Appendix A.5.3 in current rebuttal version) are actually the subset of the genes shown in Figure 4(last version, Figure 4(a) in current version). The missing genes are not in the same attention block with the marker genes presented in Figure 5, since the attention blocks are divided by uniform grouping.

Moreover, we make some modifications in our paper in the rebuttal version. Thanks for your time and advice.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper focuses on solving a supervised classification problem as well as providing interpretability, specifically in the field of single cell RNA analysis. The authors propose two models: first they propose a capsule attention network using self-attention mechanism together and show that it performs well in single cell RNA analysis. Noting that the CAN model lacks interpretability they move on to CGRAN. CGRAN uses gene embeddings and cell embeddings as input, mimicing to some degree the the structure of the Bert model. The main contribution of this paper is feature extraction/tokenizing cells and genes. In CAN model, they uses several vectors to represent the information contained in genes (the capsule concept is not the same and as complicated as the one used in CV and the origin of the idea is not mentioned in the paper). In CGRAN, it utilizes the gene embeddings as a representation of the genes scalar value.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
- In section 6.4, performance of CGRAN and CAN are comparable to SVM in all datasets.  Given that the structure of the model is much more complicated, it's not clear that either of these approaches actually improve classification performance over simpler classification methods.  The authors could also consider XGBOOST as a canonical method for tabular data.
- It's not really clear why the CAN model is presented at all.  It performs comparably to CGRAN without the ease of interpretation.  Why not just make the paper about the CGRAN model? The author does not provide the intuition and motivation for CAN.
- I had a hard time understanding figures 4 and 5.  In 4c, the genes are ordered differently from 4a/b which makes hard to tell if genes with similar attention levels.  I think these results can be displayed in a more compelling fashion, e.g. by quantifying the overlap between blocks with high co-attention and marker genes of common cell types.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
- The description about how to build capsules appears to be inconsistent with fig 1. mu is used as the number of capsule features for each capsule as well as number of fully connected layers
- As noted above, the attention weight results in Section 5.2 are compelling but are not clearly described.  This makes it hard to evaluate the utility of the model.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I think the paper tackles an important problem although I found the presentation somewhat unclear.  I'm not an expert on attention based models so I'm not 100% sure of my review, but I think the authors can certainly do a better job characterizing the classification strength of their model (e.g. over simpler alternatives like SVM) while also clearly articulating the interpretations and insights from the attention weights.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
Overview:
 - This work focuses on developing supervised cell type classification models for scRNA-seq datasets. Interpretability of classifiers is a key consideration for the proposed models. This work presents two main approaches, each using the attention mechanism as a component. 

Methods:
 - In the first approach, gene expression values are first projected into a smaller number of higher dimensional features $m$ times. Attention is used to combine the keys (from each of the $m$ projections) with values and queries (from each of the $m$ projections). Standard convolution and fully connected layers are used to predict cell type labels. 

 - In the second, independent approach to supervised classification, the authors heuristically define gene embeddings based on matrix factorization. Groups of genes are used to obtain $(k,v,q)$ projections and attention matrix. Fully connected layers are used to predict cell type labels.

Results:
 - The authors qualitatively show that for the first approach (CAN), cells with the same cell type label have similar attention patterns, which are distinct from attention patterns for cells with distinct cell type labels (Fig. 3)
 - Other qualitative results suggest that attention matrices can point to marker genes
 - Quantitative results show that the proposed methods perform marginally better than baselines considered (Tables 2 and 3)
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1. Authors identify some key issues surrounding cell type classification (domain shift, "technical" noise, ambiguity in qualifying criteria for marker genes etc.)
2. Proposed methods perform reasonably on the supervised classification task

Weakness:
1. Interpretability is not quite dealt with; this is in part because attention layers in CGRAN only work with aggregated gene sets, with each set containing 50-100 genes. 
2. The evaluation is weak. In particular, there are no error bars (cross validation), and standard classifiers (SVM) perform at par with complicated methods.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity+Quality:
- Motivation behind different components in the procedures/models is not explained well.
- Symbols are overloaded (e.g C is used to indicate capsule representations, cell embeddings, and number of cells), undefined ($\alpha$ in Figure 1 is never defined in the text), or unclear (e.g. it would be helpful to spell out dimensionality of relevant variables succinctly)
- Figure text is too small to be legible in print
- The approach is based on well-known ideas of capsule networks, dynamic routing, attention. The contribution here is adapting the methods to use features in scRNA-seq (genes), that do not inherently have a sequential structure or natural ordering, and only have a 1d measurement associated with them (gene expression value).

Novelty+Originality:
 - The approaches presented in the manuscript seem to be straightforward adaptations of well-documented ideas in the literature (capsule networks, dynamic routing, attention)
 - The experiments are in the simplest setting (individual datasets, no domain shift, always the same number of features), which don't explore raised in the introduction (ambiguity of marker genes, technical noise, use of prior knowledge etc.)
content.summary_of_the_review:
Major
 - The approaches presented in the manuscript are straightforward adaptations of well-documented ideas in the literature (capsule networks, dynamic routing, attention). I'd be happy to reconsider this point if the authors lay out specific claims to methodological innovations.
 - The authors do not demonstrated interpretability beyond a heuristically constructed qualitative agreement of their results with known marker genes.
  - The quantitative evaluation does not report any error-bars, and their classification results are on roughly equivalent to simple baselines.

Minor
 - Decision Trees are a weak baseline. Replace Random Forests with boosted versions (e.g. XGBoost), and include a comparable MLP. I'd also ensure these baselines are tuned appropriately (e.g. using an off-the-shelf hyper-parameter tuning procedure). 
 - See other points listed in the Clarity+Quality section

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The authors introduce two self-attention-based models for cell type classification, Capsule Attention Network (CAN) and Cell-Gene Representation Attention Network (CGRAN). CAN directly extends the approach introduced in [1] introducing self-attention. The second is a novel architecture that can explicitly model self-attention between genes, enabling the identification of marker genes and exploring relationships between genes. The two approaches are tested on 9 single-cell datasets and compared with other machine learning methods. Based on the reported results, their methods yield highest test accuracy for 6 out 9 datasets (3 and 3 for CAN and CGRAN, respectively).

[1] Wang L, Nie R, Yu Z, Xin R, Zheng C, Zhang Z, Zhang J, Cai J. An interpretable deep-learning architecture of capsule networks for identifying cell-type gene expression programs from single-cell RNA-sequencing data. Nature Machine Intelligence. 2020 Nov;2(11):693-703.

content.title: Replies on the review
content.comment:
Dear Reviewer,

We thank you for the time and efforts reviewing our paper. We have received some valuable and constructive feedbacks from you to improve our paper. Here we will address your concerns.


Concern 1: Many of the methods considered in the comparison paper Abdelaal et al (2019) are missing.

Reply : In our updated version, we have included ACTINN, Cell Blast, scVI and Moana listed in the paper for comparison. The benchmarking paper shows that SVM is the best among all existing methods. Since our experiment is including but not limited to SVM, XGBoost and several leading methods in the benchmarking paper, we think the comparative experiment is now adequate.



Concern 2: It is my understanding that all the methods were applied considering the top 1,000 variable genes only. However, some of the baseline methods consider a different gene/feature selection procedure (for example, ACTINN “uses all the genes to capture the features for each cell type” [1]). This could lead to suboptimal results in the author’s implementation; 

Reply : Due to computational limit, we can not input over 1500 genes. This could lead to suboptimal results for some methods operating on the whole data. However, we believe that by setting the same data input for all methods will result in a fair comparison among all methods.


Concern 3: If computationally feasible, it would be important to quantify how variable are the reported accuracy for different train/test splits of the data (e.g., quantifying mean and standard deviations of accuracy across splits). 

Reply: For each experiment, we randomly run it for three times and calculate the mean accuracy. we think providing the variance based on the three times of repeated experiments is not very convincing. We may do more experiments and provides the standard deviation in future edition.


Concern 4: I think the authors would need to show more data to demonstrate their claims about model interpretability. 

Reply : We add these illustrations in ' 5.5 The interpretation of Cell-Gene Representation Attention Network'  in the article and Appendix A.5.


Concern 5: Reproducibility. The proposed model has many hyperparameters but the authors do not comment on how they were chosen.

Reply : We detail our experiment settings in the new version. Please refer to 5.3.

Moreover, we make some modifications in our paper in the rebuttal version. Thanks for your time and advice.
